primary_scientific_question: How does downstream POLARIS EMS operational behavior change as a function of systematic forecast error in solar, wind, and demand when the frozen closed-loop MPC is supplied with perturbed forecasts under identical hidden ground-truth actual trajectories?
central_scientific_conclusion: Under the tested conditions, the frozen POLARIS EMS maintained load service despite the specified systematic forecast perturbations, while its economic and resource-dispatch behavior remained materially sensitive to forecast bias. D5 therefore characterizes forecast-to-EMS operational sensitivity rather than forecasting-model accuracy.

stage8_1_vs_d5.explicit_statement: D5 did not directly evaluate the Stage8.1 ML forecasting model.
target_hierarchy: Stage8.1 forecasting target: SW_IN (solar irradiance in W/m^2)
Physical / PV conversion semantics: P_solar = SW_IN * PV_area * PV_eff * PR (Watts)
stage8_1_vs_d5.distinction: Input feature != prediction target != forecast channel. Injected D5 perturbation != empirical ML model error.

level_1_directly_demonstrated: All six tested scenarios maintained 100% Load-Served Fraction under the specified experimental conditions.
Forecast perturbations materially change diesel consumption (-100.00% to +57.97%), diesel operating hours, renewable curtailment (-91.09% to +228.16%), and SOC trajectory behavior.
Solar overprediction (D5-2) reduces diesel fuel by 41.90 L (-48.77%) and increases curtailment by 17.96 kWh (+12.19%).
Wind underprediction (D5-3) increases diesel fuel by 46.04 L (+53.58%) and reduces curtailment by 134.20 kWh (-91.09%).
Demand overprediction (D5-4) increases diesel fuel by 49.81 L (+57.97%) and reduces curtailment by 122.15 kWh (-82.91%).
Compound optimistic perturbation (D5-5) reduces diesel fuel by 85.92 L (-100.00%) and increases curtailment by 336.14 kWh (+228.16%).
Persistent +15% renewable perturbation (D5-6) reduces 7-day fuel by 96.66 L (-40.03%) and increases curtailment by 691.36 kWh (+43.91%) over 168 closed-loop steps.
level_2_reasonable_system_interpretation: Under the tested station configuration, hidden actual trajectories, perturbation magnitudes, and durations, the configured resources maintained load service without recorded physical constraint violations.
The aggregate results are consistent with altered forecast-driven resource scheduling.
Optimistic forecast bias leads to deferred or reduced diesel commitment, increasing reliance on battery storage.
Pessimistic forecast bias leads to increased diesel commitment, increasing fuel burn and reducing curtailment.
level_3_not_established: Stage8.1 empirical model-error distribution or empirical forecast accuracy.
Stage8.1 model calibration or generalization beyond its benchmark.
Real-world forecast-error frequency or probability of +/-30% error.
Global EMS robustness or safety under arbitrary extreme weather.
Infinite-horizon control stability, universal control stability, or long-term field reliability.
Field reliability under physical component aging.
Wind forecasting performance of the solar model.

required_question_answers.q1_what_d5_tested: Controlled systematic forecast perturbations (gamma = 0.70 ... 1.30) across solar, wind, and demand channels and their downstream EMS operational consequences in a closed-loop MPC environment.
required_question_answers.q2_what_d5_observed: 100% Load-Served Fraction across all six tested scenarios, accompanied by material changes in diesel fuel consumption (-100.00% to +57.97%), diesel operating hours, renewable curtailment (-91.09% to +228.16%), and SOC trajectory dynamics.
required_question_answers.q3_did_d5_test_stage8_1_ml_accuracy: No. D5 did not directly evaluate Stage8.1 ML forecasting accuracy. The D5 runtime used LocalBaselineForecastEngine (a prototype baseline / heuristic forecast engine) and did not ingest Chronos or TimesFM prediction outputs.
required_question_answers.q4_d5_1_d5_2_relationship_to_stage8_1: They are solar-channel EMS sensitivity experiments that are conceptually relevant to the Stage8.1 solar forecasting problem (modifying the solar channel), but they do NOT evaluate Stage8.1 model accuracy or empirical model error.
required_question_answers.q5_what_are_d5_3_d5_4: EMS system-level sensitivity experiments for wind and demand forecast channels, evaluating operational sensitivity to non-solar forecast perturbations.
required_question_answers.q6_what_are_d5_5_d5_6: D5-5 is a compound optimistic forecast perturbation experiment (1.30x / 1.30x / 0.80x). D5-6 is a persistent multi-channel forecast perturbation experiment (1.15x / 1.15x) evaluated over 168 sequential closed-loop MPC steps.
required_question_answers.q7_what_remains_unproven: Empirical model error distributions, real-world error frequency, field performance under extreme unmodeled weather, global EMS robustness, universal safety, infinite-horizon control stability, wind model accuracy, and demand model accuracy.
required_question_answers.q8_where_does_wind_come_from: Wind generation (P_wind) is populated in the D5 runtime via a heuristic persistence rule (last_obs_wind + 5000 * sin(...)) in LocalBaselineForecastEngine. It is NOT an output or prediction target of the solar forecasting model.
